title: Alarm zone permanently shorted
summary: The panel reports a short (or tamper / trouble) on the zone that won't clear.
symptoms: Zone reports short circuit, or tamper / trouble on panels that treat a short that way.
The zone never changes when the detector is walk-tested or its cover is removed.
safety: Tell the monitoring centre and the site contact before testing, and put the system or zone into test/service mode under site procedure.
Photograph or label terminations before disconnecting anything.
Only measure resistance on an isolated circuit: disconnect the zone conductors from the panel first. Never use the Ω range on live terminals.
Never test by shorting supply outputs or zone inputs with a link.
Backup batteries can deliver very high fault currents: never short battery leads or terminals, and isolate the battery as well as mains before working inside a panel or power supply.

Mains (230 V) wiring is restricted electrical work — only a licensed electrician may work on it. Apprentices should do these tests under supervision and within their licence conditions; follow site procedures and the manufacturer's documentation.

nodes.text: Which EOL resistors does this zone use?
nodes.help: Generic dual EOL wiring: R1, the EOL resistor, in series with the loop; R2, the alarm resistor, across the detector's NC alarm contact; the tamper contact in series. Expected readings are calculated from the values you choose. These are examples, not values for any particular panel — and not every installation uses this wiring. If yours differs, choose 'Different wiring or not sure'.

unsupported.label: Different wiring (e.g. tamper resistor, triple EOL) or not sure
unsupported.finding: EOL wiring not known or not the generic dual EOL topology.

nodes.text: What's the history of this zone?

answers.label: It worked, and there's been recent work on site
answers.finding: Zone worked before; recent work on site.

answers.label: It worked, and nothing has changed that I know of
answers.finding: Zone worked before; no known changes.

answers.label: New installation, or the panel was recently programmed

nodes.text: What does the zone loop measure at the panel?

test.procedure: Isolate the zone: disconnect both zone conductors from the panel terminals. With the detector sealed, measure across the two conductors on the Ω range.
test.expected: About the sealed reading for the resistors you chose ({sealed}). R1 alone sets it; R2 only adds when the alarm contact opens.

nodes.safety: Resistance range only on the disconnected conductors.

ranges.label: Near 0 Ω
ranges.finding: Loop reads {value} at the panel: shorted.

ranges.label: Below the sealed reading
ranges.finding: Loop reads {value}: below the sealed reading.

ranges.label: About the sealed reading
ranges.finding: Loop reads {value}: about the sealed reading — the field wiring looks healthy when isolated.

ranges.label: Above the sealed reading but not open

nodes.text: With the cable disconnected at the detector, what do the cable conductors measure?

test.procedure: Leave the zone disconnected at the panel. At the detector, disconnect the zone cable. Measure across the two zone conductors at the panel end again: now neither end is connected to anything.
test.expected: OL — two conductors with nothing on either end should be open. A low reading means the cable itself is shorted.

nodes.safety: Both ends of the cable stay disconnected while you measure.

ranges.label: Near 0 Ω (still shorted)
ranges.finding: Cable alone reads {value}: the short is in the cable or joints.

ranges.label: Some resistance (leakage, or another device or resistor still on the cable)
ranges.finding: Cable alone reads {value}: not open — leakage, or something else still connected to the cable.

ranges.label: OL / open circuit
ranges.finding: Cable alone reads {value}: the cable is clear, so the short is at the detector end.

skip.label: I can't get to the detector

nodes.title: Confirm the zone's EOL values first
nodes.summary: This guide can only judge readings for the generic dual EOL wiring with known resistor values.
verify: Check the zone's EOL type and values in the panel programming.
Check installation records.
Measure each EOL resistor on its own with the zone isolated.
actions: Restart this guide once you know the expected values.
notes: None of the common combinations is universally correct; the panel's documentation and programming decide.

nodes.title: The short is in the cable or joints
nodes.summary: With both ends disconnected the conductors still read near 0 Ω, so they are touching somewhere along the run.
verify: Inspect joints and junction boxes, then any areas of recent work (staples, screws, crushed cable).
Split the run at an intermediate joint and measure each section to narrow down the faulty part.
actions: Repair or replace the damaged section and re-measure: the isolated cable should read OL, and with the detector reconnected, the sealed reading.
escalate: If the cable is concealed and can't be repaired, quote a recable and record any temporary arrangement.

nodes.title: The cable isn't clear on its own
nodes.summary: With both ends disconnected the cable should read OL. A resistance means leakage between conductors (moisture, damaged insulation) or another device or resistor still connected — for example at a joint.
verify: Check for resistors, devices or links left in joints or junction boxes along the run.
Check external or underground runs and damp joints for water or corrosion.
Measure each section separately to find where it comes from.
actions: Replace the affected section; use cable and joints suited to the environment.

nodes.title: The short is at the detector end
nodes.summary: The cable is clear, so the short is likely in the detector's terminations or EOL network.
verify: Check for a wire link left across the zone terminals, or both EOL resistors bypassed.
Compare the detector wiring against the panel's and detector's wiring diagrams.
Measure the detector's EOL network on its own (isolated): it should read the sealed reading.
actions: Remove the link or correct the wiring so the loop passes through the contacts and both resistors as designed.
notes: A link across zone terminals left from commissioning or a previous fault is a common cause on existing sites.

nodes.title: Short between the panel and the detector
nodes.summary: The loop is shorted, but without separating the detector the fault can't be placed in the cable or at the detector.
verify: Get access to the detector and disconnect the cable there, then re-measure the cable alone.
actions: Repair the faulty section once located.

nodes.title: The loop reads below the sealed reading
nodes.summary: Some panels report a reading below their seal band as a short. A wrong resistor or leakage is likely.
verify: Measure each EOL resistor on its own with the detector disconnected.
Check the cable alone for leakage (should read OL).
Confirm the panel's programmed EOL values.
actions: Replace wrong resistors; repair leakage; correct programming.

review.note: Whether a below-sealed reading is reported as 'short' depends on the panel's bands — panel-specific.

nodes.title: Field wiring looks healthy — check the panel end
nodes.summary: Isolated, the loop reads sealed, yet the panel reports a short. The cause is likely at the panel end, but verify first.
verify: Check the zone's EOL type and values in the panel programming (e.g. a zone set for different EOL values can read a healthy loop as short).
Check nothing else is landed on the same zone terminals.
Fit a known-good resistor equal to R1 (the sealed reading) directly on the input, with the zone conductors disconnected, and check the status.
actions: Correct programming or terminations. If a known-good resistor also reads short, report the input as faulty.
escalate: Contact the manufacturer's technical support if the input misreads a known-good resistor.

nodes.title: The loop isn't shorted when isolated
nodes.summary: The isolated loop reads above the sealed reading, not a short. The panel's report doesn't match the field wiring.
verify: Confirm how this panel reports each band (short, sealed, alarm, tamper) for the programmed EOL type.
Measure each resistor on its own.
actions: Correct the programming or resistors so the readings fall in the panel's bands.

nodes.title: The loop is open, not shorted
nodes.summary: The isolated loop reads open. Some panels report this as tamper or trouble.
verify: Follow the 'Alarm zone permanently open' guide.

nodes.title: Measurements needed
nodes.summary: Without measurements the possible causes can't be narrowed down safely.
verify: Get a multimeter: the next steps rely on isolated resistance measurements.
Meanwhile, look for links across terminals and visible cable damage.
actions: Return to this guide with a meter.

cable-short.title: Short in the cable
cable-short.detail: Conductors touching through damaged insulation — staples, screws, crushed cable — or a poorly made joint.

moisture.title: Moisture or contamination
moisture.detail: Water or corrosion in joints or damaged cable lets current leak between conductors.

wiring-error.title: Wiring error at the detector
wiring-error.detail: Conductors on the wrong terminals, or resistors wired so they are bypassed.

link-left.title: Link left across the zone
link-left.detail: A wire link fitted across the zone or EOL terminals and never removed.

detector-fault.title: Detector fault
detector-fault.detail: A failed detector whose terminals read shorted with the cable removed.

wrong-resistor.title: Wrong resistor value
wrong-resistor.detail: A lower-value resistor than intended, reading in the panel's short band.

config.title: Programming doesn't match the wiring
config.detail: EOL type or values, or zone type, in the panel don't match what's installed.

panel-input.title: Panel zone input or expander fault
panel-input.detail: The input itself misreads a healthy loop.

other-device.title: Another device on the cable
other-device.detail: A resistor, link or second device left connected part-way along the run (e.g. in a joint).

escalation: Escalate to a senior technician or the manufacturer's support if a known-good resistor on the input doesn't read sealed.
If the zone must stay isolated, tell the site contact and monitoring centre, record it, and book the return visit.
notes: 2k2 / 4k4 and 10k / 20k are generic examples. Your panel's EOL values, and how it reports open, short and tamper, depend on the manufacturer, model and programming.
Resistance is only meaningful on an isolated circuit.

pending: The ±10 % band used to call a reading 'about' the expected value allows for 5 % resistors, cable resistance and meter accuracy. It is a diagnostic aid, not any panel's alarm threshold — confirm it suits long cable runs.
Expected readings assume the generic dual EOL topology (R1 in series, R2 across the NC alarm contact, tamper in series). Confirm against the panel's and detector's wiring diagrams.
How the panel classifies low readings (short, tamper or trouble) is panel-specific.
